When the moon rises to its apex, lithe arthropods scamper across the Farplains, their powerful articulated legs propelling them quickly 
in search of sleeping prey. Th ese instinctual pack animals prowl silently, coordinating their movements through the use of pheromones. 
Searching for burrows, lone herd beasts or wayward young, once they chance upon an easy kill they encircle the prey quickly and strike 
with flight-assisted leaps; their forward tarsus claws and sharp mandibles plunging deep into flesh and chitin alike. Khanith share 
a curious relationship with the lumbering khanaur, their shared ancestry leaving echoes of a pheromone based understanding. Th is 
connection goes beyond a lack of predation, as the khanith have been seen fi ercely defending packs of khanaur from aggressors.

Scents on the Wind Th e khanith has Advantage on Wisdom 
(Perception) checks that rely on smell.
Predatory Tactics Th e khanith has Advantage on an attack rolls 
against a creature if at least one of the khanith’s allies is within 5 ft. 
of the creature and the ally isn’t incapacitated.
Distant Kin If a friendly khanith or khanaur creature is attacked 
within 60 ft., surrounding khanith become aware by the use of 
pheromones. Khanaur are considered allies to the khanith.

Encountering Th e khanith prowl silently when the night is cool 
and the moon lights the plains. When they choose to run, the 
buzzing of their wings can be heard on the wind, a sound that 
often heralds death. As beasts of primal instincts, there is little 
that can be done to inhibit their aggression to any that are not 
of their kind or the larger khanaur, which they protect with a 
fi erce ancestral bond.
